samples.summary: No test asserts that `themedDeck` actually writes the authored text into the layout's placeholders
samples.evidence: `themedDeck` fills placeholders with `texts.forEach((lines, i) => { const target = placeholders[i]; if (!target) return; ... })` (builders.ts:357-370). The `if (!target) return` silently drops any text array with no matching placeholder, and the whole substitution is skipped if `applyLayoutToSlide` yields no `placeholderRef` text elements. The only coverage for the 17 new decks is `packages/backend/src/template/seed/catalog.spec.ts`, which checks unique slide/element ids (l.247-257), listing metadata (l.56-65) and that `assertValidSlidesBody` does not throw (l.67-105). None of those inspect `slide.elements[*].data.blocks[*].inlines[*].text`, so a deck that shipped with every slide still carrying the layout's default placeholder text — or with half its bullets silently dropped — would pass the suite green. This is a user-visible gallery defect (blank/wrong templates) with zero detection.
searchedFor: Grep themedDeck|decorate|Decor|recolor in packages/backend (only builders.ts + catalog/slides-*.ts, no spec)

samples.summary: The new `decorate()` composition presets (including `recolor` contrast and sidebar/split text relocation) have no test at all
samples.evidence: `decorate()` (builders.ts:205-296) is new behavior applied to every slide of all 17 new templates: it prepends shape elements, calls `recolor(texts, 'background')` for the `block`/`gradient`/`header` presets so text stays readable over an accent fill, and mutates `t.frame.x`/`t.frame.w` for `sidebar`/`split` so text is not buried under the colour column. No spec exercises `decorate`, `recolor` or any `Decor` value (grep for `decorate|Decor|recolor` across packages/backend finds only builders.ts and the catalog data files). `catalog.spec.ts` only asserts unique ids and that `assertValidSlidesBody` passes — both hold whether or not the recolour ran or the frames moved. So a regression that leaves white-on-white text, or leaves placeholder text underneath the sidebar block, ships undetected across the whole gallery.

samples.summary: The unknown-built-in-theme guard in `themedDeck` is untested
samples.evidence: builders.ts:325-334 adds a deliberate guard (`if (resolvedTheme.id !== theme) throw new Error('Unknown built-in theme id: ...')`) precisely because `getBuiltInTheme` falls back to default-light. No test calls `themedDeck` with a bogus theme id; the only slides coverage is data-driven through `TEMPLATE_CATALOG`. The guard would in practice fail loudly at module load, so impact is contained, but nothing pins the behavior if someone later replaces the throw with the silent fallback.

samples.summary: briefs.spec checks brief→template only; nothing checks that every slides template has a brief, so a new template silently ships with no input schema
samples.evidence: `it('every brief maps to an existing slides template')` (briefs.spec.ts:10-14) iterates briefs and asserts the slug exists in the catalogue. The reverse — every `content.kind === 'slides'` seed has a `TEMPLATE_BRIEFS` entry — is never asserted. Given briefs are described as the required-values schema a fill agent looks up per template, a template added without a brief (or a brief slug renamed on one side only) is exactly the drift this file exists to prevent, and it would pass green.

samples.summary: Brief tests assert only self-consistency of the brief data; nothing ties a field's min/max (or count of fields) to the slide it is supposed to fill
samples.evidence: The suite checks unique keys, min<=max and pair length (briefs.spec.ts:21-42) — all properties of the brief object in isolation. The brief docblock (catalog/brief.ts:1-8) claims a brief declares 'exactly what to ask for and where it goes', and fields carry `min`/`max` described as 'how many rows the slide is designed for'. No test compares those row counts against the corresponding template's slide placeholder line counts, so e.g. `agenda` min 4/max 4 against a 3-line body slide would never be caught and a fill agent would silently truncate user content.
searchedFor: Grep TEMPLATE_BRIEFS consumers in packages/backend (only briefs.ts + spec)

samples.summary: Nothing asserts each new deck embeds/points at its chosen theme (meta.themeId present in `themes[]`, and distinct per template)
samples.evidence: The stated purpose of `themedDeck` (builders.ts:313-320 and packages/cli/skills/slides-author.md 'Pick a distinct theme per template') is that each template reads as a different design. `assertValidSlidesBody` only requires `meta.themeId` be a non-empty string (docs-content.controller.ts:564-570); it never checks it resolves to an entry in `themes`. catalog.spec.ts has no theme assertion. A deck whose themeId does not match any embedded theme (or 17 decks that all collapse to default-light) would ship green.

samples.summary: Brief tests would pass vacuously if TEMPLATE_BRIEFS were empty
samples.evidence: All four data-driven tests are `for (const b of TEMPLATE_BRIEFS)` loops with no assertion that the array is non-empty (contrast catalog.spec.ts:29-31 which pins `TEMPLATE_CATALOG.length > 0`). If the barrel in briefs.ts were emptied or an import dropped, every loop body would be skipped and the file would report four passes.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real. `themedDeck` (builders.ts:356-368) writes authored text into layout placeholders and silently returns when no placeholder exists (`if (!target) return`), with no runtime guard anywhere in builders.ts (only throws are for unknown layout/theme ids at l.107, 332, 342, 447). I read both specs that touch the catalogue: catalog.spec.ts covers slugs, stable ids, listing metadata, structural `assertValidSlidesBody`, sheet formulas/totals, and id uniqueness — never `slide.elements[*].data.blocks[*].inlines[*].text`; briefs.spec.ts only checks brief/slug mapping and field shape. `assertValidSlidesBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:551-591) is purely structural and would accept a deck full of layout default text. Searched wide for a counterexample and found none: repo-wide grep for `themedDeck` matches no test file; `TEMPLATE_CATALOG` is imported by only those two specs; `inlines`/`data.blocks`/`type === 'text'` in all spec/test files are unrelated (yorkie, slides package, board, frontend); backend/test/template.e2e-spec.ts is an HTTP authorization/share-link suite with no catalogue content; cli/test/templates.test.ts only checks listing types; no snapshots of seed decks; and distinctive authored strings ("What went well", "Action items") appear only in catalogue source and docs, never in a test. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a new behavior (17 new decks plus the substitution path) whose failure ships blank/default or bullet-dropped templates into the public gallery with zero detection — major, and blocking.

I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: repo-wide grep for TEMPLATE_CATALOG/themedDeck/seed-builders imports shows only catalog.spec.ts and catalog/briefs.spec.ts import the catalog; briefs.spec.ts asserts only brief metadata; template.e2e-spec.ts has no matches for shape/frame/color/accent/slides; there is no builders.spec.ts and no __snapshots__ under packages/backend.
